title: LowMC-M Non-Aligned Differential Attack Complexity
summary: The limited-birthday estimate is only a best case because the targeted sub-tweak differences are unlikely to be aligned; the actual attack complexity remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For $\mathrm{LowMC\text{-}M}$, determine the attack complexity of recovering a high-probability related-tweak differential characteristic when the targeted set of sub-tweak differences lacks suitable alignment. The existing best-case estimate uses a generic limited-birthday algorithm that assumes an admissible output-difference set aligned for maximal use of local birthday-type search. Because the targeted sub-tweak-difference set is unlikely to satisfy this assumption, the estimate does not determine the attack complexity in the non-aligned case.

scope.domain: Differential cryptanalysis of the tweakable block cipher LowMC-M.
assumptions: An admissible output-difference set is aligned for maximal use of local birthday-type search.
parameters: The targeted set of sub-tweak differences: the target set whose alignment is at issue
The admissible output-difference set: the output set whose alignment is assumed by the estimate
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the attack complexity of recovering a high-probability related-tweak differential characteristic when the targeted sub-tweak-difference set lacks suitable alignment.

citations.label: The MALICIOUS Framework: Embedding Backdoors into Tweakable Block Ciphers

progress.summary: The source presents the limited-birthday estimate as an attacker's best-case complexity because its required output-set alignment is unlikely for the targeted sub-tweak differences. It leaves the actual complexity in the non-aligned case undetermined.
